name: InMode Lumecca
lead: InMode Lumecca is an intense pulsed light (IPL) device from the aesthetics company InMode, used in clinics to improve skin tone and clarity. It is mainly offered for brown spots, sun damage, and visible redness or small surface vessels on the face, neck, chest and hands.

People use it to get a more even, clearer complexion: pigment and redness are targeted with broad-spectrum light pulses, and treated spots typically darken and flake away over the following days. Clinics commonly schedule a short series of sessions.
A registered clinical trial (2025) studied IPL, an anti-redness dermocosmetic and their combination for rosacea, which places IPL-type treatment within research on facial redness.

chain: Pulses of broad-spectrum light absorbed by pigment and blood vessels
Targeted spots and redness break down and clear
angle.text: Lumecca is used to even out skin colour by targeting sun spots, freckle-like pigment and facial redness. People book it for a clearer, more uniform complexion, often across a few sessions.

paras: Lumecca is a provider-operated IPL platform. IPL devices emit a range of light wavelengths that are absorbed by pigment (melanin) and by haemoglobin in blood vessels, which is why they are used for both brown spots and redness.
Appearance communities discuss IPL as a way to even out skin tone and reduce visible redness without peeling or surgery. Providers commonly advise sun protection before and after treatment.

Commonly reported effects of IPL in general include temporary redness, swelling, and darkening of treated spots before they fade; pigment changes and burns are among the less common risks, and recent tanning or darker skin tones are usually discussed with the provider beforehand.

A 2025 registered trial (NCT07729540, 60 participants, listed as completed) compared IPL, an anti-redness dermocosmetic and the two combined in the treatment of rosacea [1]. It does not name a specific device, and no published results for Lumecca itself are listed.

timeline.event: Trial of IPL, an anti-redness dermocosmetic and their combination in rosacea started in September [1]

card.summary: InMode Lumecca is an in-clinic IPL treatment that targets brown spots and redness for a clearer, more even complexion.
card.note: Sun protection is usually advised; temporary darkening of spots is expected.

quick.overview:
Lumecca is a light-based clinic treatment for skin tone. It is used on sun spots, uneven pigment and visible redness on the face, neck, chest and hands.

People use it for a clearer, more uniform complexion, usually in a few sessions spaced weeks apart.
quick.mechanism: Intense pulsed light delivers broad-spectrum pulses that pigment and blood vessels absorb. The targeted spots darken and flake off, and redness fades as small vessels are treated.
quick.risks: Temporary redness, swelling and spot darkening are commonly described. Pigment changes and burns are less common, and providers usually discuss tanning, skin tone and sun protection beforehand.
